what: one real case end to end: a critical examination finding the transcript establishes twice, the note records twice, and two twins remove differently

case.presenting_complaint: Left-sided chest wall pain in an office worker in their 30s, of about a week's duration, that came on after heavy lifting during a house move; sharp and positional (worse on twisting and deep breaths), with reproducible tenderness over the costochondral junctions on examination and explicit denial of cardiac features. Working diagnosis: musculoskeletal chest-wall pain / costochondritis, managed with reassurance and simple analgesia.
case.fact: Examination: palpation over the costochondral junctions reproduces the patient's pain (key positive finding)
case.provenance: authored scenario: transcript, fact sheet and repaired reference note are all ours; no vendor note text, no third-party corpus

transcript_sites.quote: when I press over these little joints where the rib cartilage meets the breastbone - we call them the costochondral junctions - I'm reproducing your pain
transcript_sites.speaker: doctor

transcript_sites.quote: crucially I can press on the spot and reproduce exactly the pain you've been getting
transcript_sites.speaker: doctor

pipeline_extraction.extracted_fact: On examination, palpation over the costochondral junctions beside the breastbone was tender and reproduced the patient's exact pain.

pipeline_extraction.audit_fact: Palpation over the costochondral junctions beside the breastbone was tender and reproduced the exact pain.

note_sites.span: Palpation over costochondral junctions reproduced patient's pain.

versions.label: clean note (verified twin)
versions.examination: Palpation over costochondral junctions reproduced patient's pain. Heart sounds normal/regular, no added sounds. Chest clear with good air entry bilaterally, no wheeze/crackles. SpO2 99%. Pulse and BP normal.
versions.impression: Musculoskeletal chest-wall pain / costochondritis. History, reproducible costochondral tenderness on examination and absence of cardiac features point to chest-wall origin; cardiac cause considered clinically unlikely.
